issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting information about the 'stock' attribute of SealSaloon: the UML snippet (class diagram) does not indicate that 'stock' is static, while the textual instructions explicitly require the 'stock' attribute to be static and final. This conflict can confuse students about whether to implement an instance-level Stock (per saloon) or a single shared static Stock, and implementing the wrong one will prevent passing tests that expect a shared static stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: update the UML in the problem statement to indicate that 'stock' is a static (shared) attribute (e.g., underline or annotate it) and explicitly state 'private static final Stock stock'. Alternatively, remove the textual requirement to make it static if the UML design was intended. Ensure the template and example solution match the clarified requirement.

issues.description: The class diagram shows acceptSupplyDelivery as a public method (+acceptSupplyDelivery), but the reference solution declares acceptSupplyDelivery as package-private static (no access modifier). This visibility mismatch between the UML/specification and the implementation can confuse students about the intended access level (public vs package-private) when they implement the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make visibility explicit and consistent: either change the solution and template to declare 'public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(...)' or update the UML/specification to indicate package-private visibility. Prefer declaring the method public in the specification and template to avoid ambiguity for students.
